svg.text: Forouzan Section 23.2 — Process-to-Process Datagram Delivery with Minimum Transport Overhead

g.text: Connectionless Service
• Zero Handshake Latency
Each user datagram is an independent entity with no relation
to previous or subsequent datagrams. No connection is opened,
maintained, or closed.
• Ideal for quick request-response queries like DNS and NTP.
• Reduces server load drastically by maintaining zero session state.
Unreliable Delivery
• Best-Effort Service Model
UDP does not guarantee delivery, packet sequencing, or loss
recovery. If a packet is corrupted in transit, the checksum detects
it and the receiver quietly discards it.
• No retransmission timers; application handles error recovery
if needed (or tolerates dropped samples as in voice calls).
Message-Oriented Service
• Preserves Message Boundaries
Unlike TCP, which provides a continuous unstructured stream of
bytes, UDP preserves datagram boundaries intact.
• If sender writes 100 bytes via sendto(), receiver reads exactly
100 bytes via recvfrom() in one single atomic operation.
• Eliminates the need for application-level record delimiters!
Multicast & Broadcast
• Flexible Transmission Modes
TCP is strictly point-to-point (unicast between 2 endpoints).
UDP inherently supports 1-to-many communication:
• Unicast: One sender to one receiver.
• Multicast: One sender to a subscribed multicast group (e.g. IPTV).
• Broadcast: One sender to all nodes on local subnet (DHCP discover).
